evidence.excerpt: Most ICS anomaly detectors are designed for a specific protocol and rely on parsed field values. This paper investigates a protocol-agnostic approach in which raw application-layer payload bytes from the first 64 bytes of each PDU are used to construct feature vectors via byte-frequency histograms augmented with bigram entropy and mean absolute deviation of byte values. A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures from a testbed running Modbus, DNP3, and a proprietary vendor protocol for which no parser was available. The proprietary protocol represented 31% of traffic. Against seven attack scenarios including vendor-protocol-specific command injection, the protocol-agnostic detectors achieved AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, compared with 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector applied only to Modbus traffic. The paper discusses cases where protocol-agnostic features are sufficient and where parsed fields remain necessary, providing a decision framework for practitioners deploying detectors on heterogeneous industrial networks.
